The prosecution case, as per the First Information Report, is that on 30.12.2017, in the evening,
the appellant, along with other accused persons, armed with lathi, farsa, daab, etc., came to the doorstep of the informant and abused her caste name and threatened to kill her family.

Upon objection, accused persons assaulted the informant and when her husband intervened the appellant Nawal Kishore Thakur @ Nawal Kishore ... vs The State Of Bihar on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195182157/

sentences.text: 1 assaulted him by means of daab (single-edged sword) on his head resulting in injury.
The co- accused Isbi Singh disrobed the informant and tried to outraged her modesty and the accused persons also took away ornaments and cash.

It has further been alleged that the reason behind the occurrence is that accused Isbi Singh took a sum of Rs. 1,99,000/- for registering land in favour of the informant's husband, but he did not execute the same.

4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the appellant has not committed any offence in the manner alleged and he has falsely been implicated in this case with ulterior motive on account of previous enmity due to land dispute.
He next submits that there is general and omnibus allegation of taking caste name of the informant Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.5056 of 2024(2) dt.12-11-2024 against the appellant and prima facie SC/ST Act is not attracted inasmuch as caste based abused has not been made in full public view.

He further submits that the appellant was given benefit of Section 41 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and subsequently charge-sheet was submitted, however, learned Magistrate took cognizance under Section 3 (i)(r)(s) of the SC/ST Act.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the learned Special Court has taken cognizance under the provisions of the of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, finding prima facie case against the appellant and in view of the decision of the Supreme Court, in the case of Bachu Das v. The State of Bihar and Others, reported in (2014) 3 SCC 471, this appeal, for grant of anticipatory bail, is not maintainable.
